real_conflicts: The proposal to 'differentiate the four secondary cards based on their category' by varying backgrounds, fonts, and alignment (Variety) directly increases cognitive load. It forces the eye to re-learn the reading pattern for every single card, destroying the effortless scanning rhythm required for a compact grid.
accepted: The proposal to move the orange circle to the negative space and reduce the opacity of the wavy lines (Simplicity) is essential and fully compatible with the other goals.
The proposal to unify the right-hand column with a consistent dark teal background (Unity) supports legibility by reducing visual fragmentation in the sidebar.
concession: I concede that the secondary cards are currently too uniform, but I reject the solution of changing their internal structure. I can accept a very subtle variation in the *category label* color or a slight change in the *left-border* thickness to provide the requested 'distinctiveness' without breaking the visual grid.
compromise: Keep the four secondary cards structurally identical (same white background, same font, same alignment) to maintain low cognitive load. To satisfy the 'variety' mandate, strictly limit the differentiation to the color of the left-border accent and the category label text color. This provides a 'cultural' visual cue without disrupting the legibility of the titles and bylines.
nonnegotiable: The feature story's text must be 100% legible; no decorative SVG element may overlap or strike through the title or excerpt text.
